name: Turbo-expander NGL recovery (GSP, RSV processes)
principle: Dry gas is chilled against cold residue gas, then expanded through a turbo-expander, which cools it further and drives a recompressor. A demethaniser column separates methane-rich residue gas from the natural gas liquids. Ortloff variants such as GSP and RSV use subcooled reflux or recycled residue gas to raise ethane recovery, and can switch to ethane rejection while keeping propane recovery high.

process_steps.name: Treated, dried gas
equipment: upstream amine and molecular sieve units

performance.metric: product recovery, Ortloff ultra-high recovery processes
performance.basis: Honeywell UOP brochure (more than 99%); flexible processes keep 99%+ propane recovery in ethane rejection

source.note: Honeywell UOP Ortloff NGL recovery brochure, UOP8424, April 2019

suppliers.name: Honeywell UOP Ortloff
suppliers.product: GSP, RSV, SCORE, SRP, SRC, SRX

advantages: Can switch between ethane recovery and rejection
Ortloff designs used in more than 90% of North American expander plants over the past decade (vendor claim)
limitations: Needs deep dehydration and CO2 control to avoid freezing
Recovery depends on inlet pressure and composition
